title: expect() waits for you
brief:
Search the shop for **dress** and prove the results arrived.

1. type `dress` into the search box (`#search_product` - it has no label, so an id is the right handle)
2. click the search button (`#submit_search`)
3. assert the **Searched Products** heading is visible

The shop takes **600 ms** to answer, and while it is thinking the product grid is empty. You will not need to do anything about that - which is the point of the challenge.
starter:
from playwright.sync_api import Page, expect


def test_search_shows_the_results_heading(page: Page):
    page.goto("https://automationexercise.com/products")

    # 1. type the search term

    # 2. click search

    # 3. assert the results heading appeared
solution:
from playwright.sync_api import Page, expect


def test_search_shows_the_results_heading(page: Page):
    page.goto("https://automationexercise.com/products")

    page.locator("#search_product").fill("dress")
    page.locator("#submit_search").click()

    expect(page.get_by_role("heading", name="Searched Products")).to_be_visible()

checks.label: The shop actually ran a search for "dress"
checks.feedback: The shop did not finish a search for "dress". Check that you filled the box before clicking, and that your test waited long enough for the results - which expect() does for you.

checks.name: to_be_visible
checks.label: You assert the results heading is visible
Your test waited out the shop's 600 ms response
checks.feedback: Your test finished before the results could possibly have arrived. That means nothing actually waited - an assertion that passes at 0 ms is not looking at the search results.

hints.label: Nudge
hints.text: .fill("dress") on the box, .click() on the button, then one expect(). No waiting code of any kind.

hints.label: Strategy
hints.text: The heading is a heading, so get_by_role("heading", name="Searched Products") reads best. Before the search it says "All Products"; afterwards it says "Searched Products".

reveal:
Look at the **page time used** figure under the results: 600 ms.

Your test waited exactly as long as the shop took - not a fixed guess, not zero. You wrote no waiting code at all; `to_be_visible()` retried until the heading turned up.

That is the whole argument against `time.sleep(2)`. A sleep would have waited 2000 ms for a 600 ms operation, and would still have been too short the day the shop got slower.
